paper.title_en: Role of \(K_{0}^{*}(700)\) exchange in the \(p\overline{p}\rightarrow\Lambda\overline{\Lambda}\) reaction
paper.abstract_en: Based on the effective Lagrangian approach, we investigate the <math display="inline"><mi>p</mi><mover accent="true"><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">¯</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><mo stretchy="false">¯</mo></mover></math> reaction. Within this framework, we provide a dynamical explanation by analyzing its total and differential cross sections, as well as the polarization of the produced <math display="inline"><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi></math> hyperon. Incorporating the <math display="inline"><mi>t</mi></math>-channel exchange of the scalar <math display="inline"><msubsup><mi>K</mi><mn>0</mn><mo>*</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>700</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math> and pseudoscalar <math display="inline"><mi>K</mi></math> mesons, complemented by an <math display="inline"><mi>s</mi></math>-channel contribution from the vector excited state, we can reproduce the current experimental data fairly well in a wide energy region. Compared to the conventional <math display="inline"><mi>K</mi></math> and <math display="inline"><msup><mi>K</mi><mo>*</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>892</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math> mesons exchange, the <math display="inline"><msubsup><mi>K</mi><mn>0</mn><mo>*</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>700</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math> meson exchange plays a more essential role in simultaneously capturing the observed features of the total and differential cross sections. The introduction of the vector <math display="inline"><mi>s</mi></math>-channel resonance improves the description of the spin observables. This work gives a perspective to inspect the role of <math display="inline"><msubsup><mi>K</mi><mn>0</mn><mo>*</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>700</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math> and serves as a test to search for the resonances in the reaction <math display="inline"><mi>p</mi><mover accent="true"><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">¯</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><mo stretchy="false">¯</mo></mover></math> at threshold.
